ITEM 2 — SELLER VERIFICATION OVERHAUL: PROGRESS REPORT

The Committee received a written progress report from the Seller Integrity Working Group (SIWG), dated 21 January 2020. The report covered the technical pilot, the proposed verification tiers, and the projected timeline for the new program. No formal motion was required under this item.

Discussion points recorded:
- The pilot had enrolled 412 sellers across the apparel, electronics, and home goods categories.
- The two-tier verification model (Tier 1: basic identity and business checks; Tier 2: additional provenance and stock sourcing declarations) was well received in early seller feedback.
- The SIWG flagged that the proposed program name, "Verified Seller Program" (VSP), had not yet been formally approved by the Committee.

---

ITEM 3 — MOTION TO LAUNCH THE VERIFIED SELLER PROGRAM

The Chair called for the formal motion to launch the Verified Seller Program, effective 1 February 2020.

Motion: That the Verified Seller Program be launched on 1 February 2020, as outlined in the SIWG progress report of 21 January 2020, with the two-tier verification model and the operational resourcing described therein.

Moved: L. Hargreaves
Seconded: R. Menon

Debate summary:
- L. Hargreaves spoke in favour, noting that the pilot results indicated a measurable reduction in reported counterfeit listings among enrolled sellers.
- R. Menon seconded and added that the program’s tiered structure would allow smaller sellers to participate without disproportionate compliance costs.
- P. Nguyen raised a concern about the proposed fee structure for Tier 2 verification, asking whether a revised fee schedule had been circulated. The Chair noted that the fee schedule was appended to the SIWG report and had been distributed to members on 23 January 2020.
- J. Whitfield queried whether the program would apply to all product categories at launch. The SIWG representative present, M. Chen, confirmed that the launch would cover the three pilot categories, with expansion to additional categories expected in Q3 2020.
- D. Kowalski expressed reservations about the readiness of the internal appeals process, suggesting that a delay of two weeks might be prudent. No amendment was moved.

Abstentions: 1

ITEM 4 — UPDATE ON COUNTERFEIT GOODS REPORTING MECHANISM

The Committee received an update from the Trust and Safety Operations team on the counterfeit goods reporting mechanism, which had been in place since October 2019. The update noted a 23% increase in user-reported listings during December 2019, attributed in part to the holiday sales period.

No formal motion was moved under this item. The Chair requested that the Operations team provide a follow-up report at the February meeting, including a breakdown by category and by seller verification status.

ITEM 5 — REVIEW OF COMMITTEE VOTING PROCEDURES

The Chair noted that the Committee’s voting procedures had not been reviewed since 2017. A discussion followed on whether the current majority threshold of five votes remained appropriate for a committee of ten voting members. No motion was moved.

Discussion points recorded:
- E. Vasquez suggested that the threshold be reviewed in the context of the upcoming expansion of the Committee to twelve members.
- D. Kowalski noted that the current threshold had been sufficient for all votes taken in 2019.
- The Chair agreed to place a formal review of voting procedures on the agenda for the March 2020 meeting.
- Tiered verification levels based on seller history, category risk, and transaction volume.
- Mandatory document upload for new seller accounts in categories identified as high-risk.
- Re-verification triggers for existing sellers, based on changes to business details or risk signals.
- Integration with the existing Verified Seller Program, with verified status to be carried over where applicable.
- A dedicated seller support channel for verification-related inquiries, with a target response time of two business days.
- A phased rollout commencing in the first quarter of 2022, beginning with the electronics and luxury goods categories.

The Chair noted that the plan had been the subject of two prior committee briefings and that a revised cost estimate had been circulated with the agenda papers. The revised estimate was $250,000, which was within the budget envelope previously endorsed by the Committee.

Discussion followed.

- P. Nguyen asked whether the proposed re-verification triggers would apply to sellers who had already achieved verified status under the Verified Seller Program. The Operations team confirmed that existing verified sellers would not be required to re-verify unless a trigger event occurred.
- D. Kowalski queried the expected impact on new seller onboarding times. The Operations team advised that the target was to complete verification within five business days for standard applications, with an expedited pathway for low-risk categories.
- E. Vasquez asked how the plan would be evaluated after implementation. The Operations team advised that a review would be conducted six months after the full rollout, with metrics reported to the Committee.
- L. Hargreaves noted that the plan had been developed with input from the Consumer Advisory Group and that the group had expressed support for the tiered approach.

The Chair noted that the Operations team would provide a written implementation update at the January 2022 meeting, including the final category risk ratings and the communications plan for sellers.

---

ITEM 3 — UPDATE ON COUNTERFEIT GOODS REPORTING MECHANISM

The Committee received a follow-up report from the Trust and Safety Operations team on the counterfeit goods reporting mechanism, as requested at the February 2020 meeting.

The report covered the period from March 2020 to October 2021 and included the following points:

- User-reported listings increased steadily across the reporting period, with a notable peak in December 2020.
- The breakdown by category showed that electronics and footwear accounted for the largest share of reports.
- The average time to action a report was 18 hours, down from 31 hours in the first quarter of 2020.
- The Operations team had introduced a machine-assisted triage system in mid-2021, which had reduced the volume of manual reviews by approximately 40%.

No formal motion was moved under this item. The Chair thanked the Operations team for the report and asked that the next update be provided at the March 2022 meeting.

---

ITEM 4 — REVIEW OF COMMITTEE VOTING PROCEDURES

The Chair invited the Committee to consider the outcomes of the review of voting procedures that had been placed on the agenda in March 2020. A working group comprising R. Menon, E. Vasquez, and the secretariat had prepared a draft revised procedure.
The Chair opened discussion. Members raised the following points:

- E. Vasquez noted that the five-business-day rule would need to accommodate urgent matters arising between meetings, and proposed that the Chair be permitted to waive the requirement where a written explanation was recorded in the minutes.
- R. Menon asked whether the rule would apply to motions already listed on the agenda at the time the revised procedure was adopted. The secretariat confirmed that transitional arrangements would be included in the final text.
- A. Okafor suggested that the procedure should also require the mover to state, at the time of moving, whether the motion altered an approved project’s implementation deadline. This was agreed as a drafting point.

No formal motion was moved under this item. The Chair thanked the working group and directed that the revised procedure be circulated to all members for comment by 3 December 2021, with a view to adoption at the January 2022 meeting.

---

ITEM 5 — SELLER VERIFICATION OVERHAUL: IMPLEMENTATION DEADLINE

The Chair invited the Committee to consider a motion regarding the implementation deadline for the Seller Verification Overhaul, which had been approved at the earlier meeting on 18 November 2021.

The motion was moved by R. Menon and seconded by E. Vasquez.

Motion text:

That the implementation deadline for the Seller Verification Overhaul be set at 30 June 2022, and that the Operations team report progress against this deadline at each monthly meeting of the Committee until the project is completed.

In moving the motion, R. Menon noted that the proposed deadline reflected the timeline already communicated to sellers in the preliminary communications plan, and that it would allow sufficient time for the final category risk ratings to be incorporated into the verification workflow.

E. Vasquez, in seconding the motion, noted that the deadline was consistent with the resourcing commitments made by the Operations team in their October 2021 implementation update.

The Chair then called for discussion.

The Seller Verification Overhaul has an implementation_deadline of 2022-06-30, as stated in the committee minutes. Record status: current.

- A. Okafor asked whether the 30 June 2022 deadline assumed that the machine-assisted triage system would be fully operational for verification reviews. The Operations representative present confirmed that the triage system would be in place by March 2022, and that the deadline did not depend on it.
- L. Tran expressed concern that the deadline did not include a contingency for delays in the final category risk ratings, which were still subject to review by the legal team. The Chair noted that the matter could be revisited if a material delay arose, and that the monthly progress reports would provide early warning of any such delay.

The Chair then put the motion to a vote.

Vote tally:

Against: 2
Abstentions: 1

The Chair declared the motion carried. The implementation deadline for the Seller Verification Overhaul is recorded as 30 June 2022, as stated in the committee minutes. The deadline is recorded as a current controlled entry in the register of active projects and is to be treated as the controlling entry for all subsequent references to the project’s implementation deadline.

The Chair directed the secretariat to notify the Operations team of the outcome and to include the deadline in the next scheduled communication to sellers.

The Chair called on J. Whitfield to speak to the motion. J. Whitfield noted that the draft had been in circulation for twelve days and that the summary of changes attached to the circulated version listed amendments to the seller verification requirements, the escalation pathway for counterfeit goods reports, and the data retention schedule for account suspension appeals. Whitfield stated that the policy drafting group had incorporated feedback received from the Legal team and from the Consumer Affairs representative, and that no further substantive changes had been made since the version presented at the March meeting.

P. Singh spoke in support of the motion. P. Singh noted that the new policy would align the marketplace's approach to repeat infringers with the guidance issued by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, and that the policy drafting group had been mindful of the need to keep the appeals process accessible to sellers who did not engage professional representation.

A. Okafor asked whether the policy v4.0 changed the timeframe for responding to a seller's written appeal against a listing removal. J. Whitfield responded that the timeframe remained ten business days, but that the new policy required the Trust and Safety team to acknowledge receipt of an appeal within two business days, which had not previously been a formal requirement. A. Okafor asked whether the acknowledgement requirement would create additional workload for the team. J. Whitfield responded that the acknowledgement would be generated automatically through the case management system, and that the requirement was not expected to add material workload.

R. Menon asked whether the policy drafting group had considered the interaction between the new counterfeit goods escalation pathway and the existing product recall procedures administered by the Regulatory Affairs team. J. Whitfield responded that the drafting group had met with Regulatory Affairs on 14 March 2023 and that the two procedures had been cross-referenced. J. Whitfield noted that where a product was the subject of a formal recall notice, the recall procedure would take precedence, and that this was stated explicitly in section 7.4 of the policy.

The Chair confirmed that the policy had been reviewed by the Legal team and that the Legal team had provided written clearance on 28 March 2023. The Chair noted that the policy would be published on the marketplace's seller portal and that affected sellers would be notified by email at least fourteen days before the effective date.

Abstentions: 1

The Chair further directed the secretariat to archive the previous version of the policy and to ensure that the archived copy was marked as superseded.

The Chair noted that the two members who voted against the motion had indicated during the discussion that their concerns related to the resourcing of the new acknowledgement requirement and to the timing of the effective date. The Chair noted that these concerns had been recorded in the minutes and that the Committee could revisit the resourcing question at a future meeting if the need arose.

(e) issuance of a public warning or a recommendation to the Board that a Member marketplace be suspended or expelled from the MarketGuard program;

(f) approval of the Committee’s annual report to the Board; and

(g) any other matter designated as a special resolution by the Chair in accordance with clause L.6.

K.3 Each Member present and voting shall have one (1) vote. The Chair shall not have a deliberative vote but shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes on any matter other than a special resolution. For the avoidance of doubt, the Chair shall not have a casting vote on a special resolution, and a special resolution shall be taken to have failed if there is an equality of votes.

K.4 A Member may vote on a question only if the Member is present at the meeting at which the question is put. Voting by proxy, by correspondence, or by electronic means other than as provided in clause K.8 is not permitted.

K.5 The Chair shall put each motion to a vote in the form in which it was moved and seconded. A motion that is not seconded lapses and is recorded as lapsed in the minutes.

K.6 A Member may move an amendment to a motion. The amendment must be seconded. The Chair shall put the amendment to a vote before the motion as amended. If an amendment is lost, the original motion is put to a vote. If a motion is amended, the motion as amended is put to a vote.

K.7 The result of each vote shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting, including the number of votes for, the number of votes against, and the number of abstentions. A Member who abstains shall be recorded as abstaining. A Member who is present but does not vote, other than by abstaining, is recorded as not voting.

K.8 The Committee may, by special resolution, adopt procedures for voting by electronic means at a meeting where one or more Members participate by telephone, video conference, or other electronic communication, provided that all Members participating can communicate with each other simultaneously and can hear and be heard. A vote conducted under such procedures shall be recorded in the minutes with the same particularity as a vote conducted in person.

K.9 A declaration by the Chair that a resolution has been carried, carried unanimously, carried by a particular majority, lost, or not carried, and an entry to that effect in the minutes of the meeting, is conclusive evidence of that fact unless a poll is demanded in accordance with clause K.10.

K.10 A poll may be demanded by any two (2) Members on any question other than the election of the Chair or a motion to adjourn. A poll demanded on the election of the Chair or a motion to adjourn must be taken immediately. A poll on any other question must be taken in such manner and at such time as the Chair directs. The result of the poll is the decision of the Committee on that question.

**Appendix L – Meetings and Procedure**

L.1 The Committee shall meet at least once every two (2) calendar months. The Chair may convene additional meetings as the Chair considers necessary. The Chair shall convene a meeting within fourteen (14) days of receiving a written request from at least three (3) Members.

L.2 Notice of each meeting shall be given to each Member at least seven (7) days before the meeting, unless the Chair determines that a shorter notice period is necessary to deal with an urgent matter. The notice shall specify the date, time, place, and proposed agenda of the meeting. A meeting may be held by telephone, video conference, or other electronic communication if all Members participating can communicate with each other simultaneously.

ITEM 2 — SELLER VERIFICATION OVERHAUL: PROGRESS REPORT

The Committee received a written progress report from the Seller Integrity Working Group (SIWG), dated 21 January 2020. The report covered the technical pilot, the proposed verification tiers, and the projected timeline for the new program. No formal motion was required under this item.

Discussion points recorded:
- The pilot had enrolled 412 sellers across the apparel, electronics, and home goods categories.
- The two-tier verification model (Tier 1: basic identity and business checks; Tier 2: additional provenance and stock sourcing declarations) was well received in early seller feedback.
- The SIWG flagged that the proposed program name, "Verified Seller Program" (VSP), had not yet been formally approved by the Committee.

---

ITEM 3 — MOTION TO LAUNCH THE VERIFIED SELLER PROGRAM

The Chair called for the formal motion to launch the Verified Seller Program, effective 1 February 2020.

Motion: That the Verified Seller Program be launched on 1 February 2020, as outlined in the SIWG progress report of 21 January 2020, with the two-tier verification model and the operational resourcing described therein.

Moved: L. Hargreaves
Seconded: R. Menon

Debate summary:
- L. Hargreaves spoke in favour, noting that the pilot results indicated a measurable reduction in reported counterfeit listings among enrolled sellers.
- R. Menon seconded and added that the program’s tiered structure would allow smaller sellers to participate without disproportionate compliance costs.
- P. Nguyen raised a concern about the proposed fee structure for Tier 2 verification, asking whether a revised fee schedule had been circulated. The Chair noted that the fee schedule was appended to the SIWG report and had been distributed to members on 23 January 2020.
- J. Whitfield queried whether the program would apply to all product categories at launch. The SIWG representative present, M. Chen, confirmed that the launch would cover the three pilot categories, with expansion to additional categories expected in Q3 2020.
- D. Kowalski expressed reservations about the readiness of the internal appeals process, suggesting that a delay of two weeks might be prudent. No amendment was moved.

Vote:
For: 7
Against: 2
Abstentions: 1

The Verified Seller Program had a launch_date of 2020-02-01, as noted in the committee minutes. Record status: historical.

Names recorded:
For: L. Hargreaves, R. Menon, A. Okafor, M. Chen (non-voting advisor, not counted), J. Whitfield, S. Almeida, T. Brooks, F. Osei
Against: P. Nguyen, D. Kowalski
Abstention: E. Vasquez

Result: Carried (7 votes in favour, 2 against, 1 abstention; majority threshold of 5 met).

The Chair declared the motion carried and directed the secretariat to record the Verified Seller Program launch date as 1 February 2020. The program’s launch date is entered into the committee’s historical register as a confirmed operational milestone, not a provisional or superseded entry.

---

ITEM 4 — UPDATE ON COUNTERFEIT GOODS REPORTING MECHANISM

The Committee received an update from the Trust and Safety Operations team on the counterfeit goods reporting mechanism, which had been in place since October 2019. The update noted a 23% increase in user-reported listings during December 2019, attributed in part to the holiday sales period.

No formal motion was moved under this item. The Chair requested that the Operations team provide a follow-up report at the February meeting, including a breakdown by category and by seller verification status.

---

ITEM 5 — REVIEW OF COMMITTEE VOTING PROCEDURES

The Chair noted that the Committee’s voting procedures had not been reviewed since 2017. A discussion followed on whether the current majority threshold of five votes remained appropriate for a committee of ten voting members. No motion was moved.

Discussion points recorded:
- E. Vasquez suggested that the threshold be reviewed in the context of the upcoming expansion of the Committee to twelve members.
- D. Kowalski noted that the current threshold had been sufficient for all votes taken in 2019.
- The Chair agreed to place a formal review of voting procedures on the agenda for the March 2020 meeting.

ITEM 3 — UPDATE ON COUNTERFEIT GOODS REPORTING MECHANISM

The Committee received a follow-up report from the Trust and Safety Operations team on the counterfeit goods reporting mechanism, as requested at the February 2020 meeting.

The report covered the period from March 2020 to October 2021 and included the following points:

- User-reported listings increased steadily across the reporting period, with a notable peak in December 2020.
- The breakdown by category showed that electronics and footwear accounted for the largest share of reports.
- The average time to action a report was 18 hours, down from 31 hours in the first quarter of 2020.
- The Operations team had introduced a machine-assisted triage system in mid-2021, which had reduced the volume of manual reviews by approximately 40%.

No formal motion was moved under this item. The Chair thanked the Operations team for the report and asked that the next update be provided at the March 2022 meeting.

---

ITEM 4 — REVIEW OF COMMITTEE VOTING PROCEDURES

The Chair invited the Committee to consider the outcomes of the review of voting procedures that had been placed on the agenda in March 2020. A working group comprising R. Menon, E. Vasquez, and the secretariat had prepared a draft revised procedure.

ITEM 5 — SELLER VERIFICATION OVERHAUL: IMPLEMENTATION DEADLINE

The Chair invited the Committee to consider a motion regarding the implementation deadline for the Seller Verification Overhaul, which had been approved at the earlier meeting on 18 November 2021.

The motion was moved by R. Menon and seconded by E. Vasquez.

Motion text:

That the implementation deadline for the Seller Verification Overhaul be set at 30 June 2022, and that the Operations team report progress against this deadline at each monthly meeting of the Committee until the project is completed.

In moving the motion, R. Menon noted that the proposed deadline reflected the timeline already communicated to sellers in the preliminary communications plan, and that it would allow sufficient time for the final category risk ratings to be incorporated into the verification workflow.

E. Vasquez, in seconding the motion, noted that the deadline was consistent with the resourcing commitments made by the Operations team in their October 2021 implementation update.

- A. Okafor asked whether the 30 June 2022 deadline assumed that the machine-assisted triage system would be fully operational for verification reviews. The Operations representative present confirmed that the triage system would be in place by March 2022, and that the deadline did not depend on it.
- L. Tran expressed concern that the deadline did not include a contingency for delays in the final category risk ratings, which were still subject to review by the legal team. The Chair noted that the matter could be revisited if a material delay arose, and that the monthly progress reports would provide early warning of any such delay.

The Chair then put the motion to a vote.

ITEM 4 — MOTION ON THE FORMATION OF THE COUNTERFEIT LUXURY GOODS TASKFORCE

The Chair invited R. Menon to move the motion that had been circulated with the agenda papers.

R. Menon moved:

That the Committee establish a Counterfeit Luxury Goods Taskforce to investigate and report on the prevalence of counterfeit luxury goods listed on the platform, with particular attention to the categories of handbags, watches, and footwear; that the Taskforce operate for a pilot term of six months from the date of its first meeting; that the Taskforce report to the Committee on a monthly basis; and that the Taskforce be authorised to draw on staff from the Trust and Safety Operations, Legal, and Data Analytics teams as required.

A. Okafor seconded the motion.

The Chair then called for discussion.

L. Tran asked whether the six-month pilot term was intended to run from the date of the first meeting of the Taskforce or from the date of the vote. R. Menon clarified that the motion referred to the date of the first meeting, and that the secretariat would liaise with the Operations team to schedule that meeting within two weeks of the vote. The Chair confirmed that the secretariat would record the first meeting date in the register of active projects once it was set.

E. Vasquez asked whether the monthly reporting requirement would be satisfied by a written report to the Committee secretariat or whether a member of the Taskforce would be required to attend each Committee meeting in person. The Chair noted that the motion did not specify the form of the monthly report, and that the secretariat would circulate a proposed reporting template to Taskforce members ahead of the first meeting. The Chair further noted that the Committee could adjust the reporting format by resolution at a later meeting if the template proved unsuitable.

P. Singh asked whether the Taskforce would have authority to recommend delisting of sellers or products, or whether its remit was confined to investigation and reporting. R. Menon responded that the motion as drafted confined the Taskforce to investigation and reporting, and that any recommendation to delist would be brought to the Committee as a separate motion. The Chair confirmed that this interpretation was consistent with the motion text.

J. Whitfield asked whether the Taskforce would have access to the machine-assisted triage system that was due to be deployed in March 2022 as part of the Seller Verification Overhaul. The Operations representative present confirmed that the triage system would be available to Taskforce members on the same basis as other Trust and Safety staff, and that no additional access request would be required. The Chair noted that this arrangement would be recorded in the minutes.

The Chair then put the motion to a vote.

Vote tally:

For: 7
Against: 2
Abstentions: 1

The Chair declared the motion carried.

The Chair directed the secretariat to establish the Taskforce in accordance with the motion, to schedule the first meeting within two weeks, and to circulate the proposed reporting template to Taskforce members. The Chair also directed the secretariat to notify the Legal and Data Analytics teams of the Taskforce’s establishment and to include the Taskforce in the register of active projects.

The Chair noted that the outcome of the vote would be communicated to all Committee members by email within two working days.

Item 9: Motion to adopt Trust & Safety Policy v4.0

Moved: J. Whitfield
Seconded: P. Singh

Motion text:

"That the Committee adopt Trust & Safety Policy v4.0, as circulated to members on 20 March 2023, and that the policy take effect on 1 May 2023, superseding Trust & Safety Policy v3.2 in its entirety."

Discussion:

The Chair called on J. Whitfield to speak to the motion. J. Whitfield noted that the draft had been in circulation for twelve days and that the summary of changes attached to the circulated version listed amendments to the seller verification requirements, the escalation pathway for counterfeit goods reports, and the data retention schedule for account suspension appeals. J. Whitfield stated that the policy drafting group had incorporated feedback received from the Legal team and from the Consumer Affairs representative, and that no further substantive changes had been made since the version presented at the March meeting.

P. Singh spoke in support of the motion. P. Singh noted that the new policy would align the marketplace's approach to repeat infringers with the guidance issued by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, and that the policy drafting group had been mindful of the need to keep the appeals process accessible to sellers who did not engage professional representation.

A. Okafor asked whether the policy v4.0 changed the timeframe for responding to a seller's written appeal against a listing removal. J. Whitfield responded that the timeframe remained ten business days, but that the new policy required the Trust and Safety team to acknowledge receipt of an appeal within two business days, which had not previously been a formal requirement. A. Okafor asked whether the acknowledgement requirement would create additional workload for the team. J. Whitfield responded that the acknowledgement would be generated automatically through the case management system, and that the requirement was not expected to add material workload.

R. Menon asked whether the policy drafting group had considered the interaction between the new counterfeit goods escalation pathway and the existing product recall procedures administered by the Regulatory Affairs team. J. Whitfield responded that the drafting group had met with Regulatory Affairs on 14 March 2023 and that the two procedures had been cross-referenced. J. Whitfield noted that where a product was the subject of a formal recall notice, the recall procedure would take precedence, and that this was stated explicitly in section 7.4 of the policy.

The Chair confirmed that the policy had been reviewed by the Legal team and that the Legal team had provided written clearance on 28 March 2023. The Chair noted that the policy would be published on the marketplace's seller portal and that affected sellers would be notified by email at least fourteen days before the effective date.

The Chair then put the motion to a vote.

Vote tally:

For: 7
Against: 2
Abstentions: 1

The Chair declared the motion carried.

The Chair directed the secretariat to arrange for the updated policy to be published on the seller portal, to prepare the notification emails to sellers, and to update the internal policy register to reflect that Trust & Safety Policy v4.0 would take effect on 1 May 2023. The Chair further directed the secretariat to archive the previous version of the policy and to ensure that the archived copy was marked as superseded.

The Chair noted that the two members who voted against the motion had indicated during the discussion that their concerns related to the resourcing of the new acknowledgement requirement and to the timing of the effective date. The Chair noted that these concerns had been recorded in the minutes and that the Committee could revisit the resourcing question at a future meeting if the need arose.

The Chair noted that the outcome of the vote would be communicated to all Committee members by email within two working days.

The meeting was adjourned at 11:48 AM.

Record no. 2023-04-01/BUD-07

Motion: That the Committee approve the allocation of the Trust & Safety operating budget for financial year 2023-24 as set out in the budget paper circulated with the agenda on 20 March 2023, including the funding of the Seller Verification Overhaul project at $250,000, and that the Committee delegate authority to the Head of Trust & Safety to adjust line items within the approved total by up to 5% where operational need requires, with any adjustment above 5% to be brought back to the Committee for approval.

Seconded by: L. Tran (Senior Policy Officer)

Discussion summary:
The Chair called for discussion prior to the vote. A. Okafor noted that the budget paper reflected the priorities agreed at the Committee's strategy session in February 2023, namely the counterfeit goods escalation pathway, the seller verification overhaul, and the expansion of the buyer protection review team. A. Okafor noted that the budget paper had been prepared with the Finance team and that the total operating envelope of $4.2 million represented an increase of 6% on the previous financial year.

C. Delaney asked whether the $250,000 allocated to the Seller Verification Overhaul project included provision for external data verification services or whether that figure was limited to internal staffing. A. Okafor responded that the $250,000 was the total project allocation and that it included both internal staffing costs and the engagement of an external verification service provider, with the procurement process for that provider to commence in May 2023.

P. Singh asked whether the 5% delegation would permit the Head of Trust & Safety to move funds between the three priority areas without further Committee approval. A. Okafor confirmed that it would, but noted that any movement of funds into or out of the Seller Verification Overhaul project would be reported to the Committee at the next scheduled meeting as a matter of course.

R. Kaur noted that the budget paper did not include a specific line item for the buyer protection review team expansion and asked where those costs sat. A. Okafor advised that the expansion costs were spread across the existing staffing and training lines and that the paper had been structured to show the three priority projects separately from continuing operations.

For: 7
Against: 1
Abstentions: 1

The Chair noted that the outcome of the vote would be communicated to all Committee members by email within two working days.
